headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared filesystem and file-processing create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of tighter isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads and writes files in a local development environment, and Agent B processes documents from files. If B ingests A-produced content, malicious instructions embedded in documents or outputs can cross the boundary. The pair lacks stated isolation or provenance tracking, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes files generated by Agent A without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace directory, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Add provenance tags to all exchanged files.
Require manual review before B parses A outputs.
Use read-only mounts for B where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before document ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles configuration secrets and academic materials, while Agent B processes documents and text. A shared filesystem or handoff of files could expose sensitive content from A to B’s processing path. No explicit isolation or redaction is documented, so leakage is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Agent A writes secrets or paper metadata into shared files, Agent B can read them.
IF Agent B is pointed at A's workspace, document contents may be ingested into B outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Mount only the minimum input folder into B.
Redact secrets before any file handoff.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: add automatic secret scanning on file exchange.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, so concurrent modification of shared files is a realistic conflict path. Agent A also runs via docker compose in a local development environment, while Agent B runs in a docker container; no locking or shared-state guarantees are stated. That makes write contention plausible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, writes can race or overwrite each other.
IF either agent mutates shared artifacts without locks, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared files.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces RAG and agentic outputs, and Agent B is a document-processing system that may treat incoming text as structured content. If B consumes A’s outputs without verification, A’s errors can cascade into downstream parsing or actions. No built-in verification step is documented for the pair, so the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A outputs as authoritative input, errors propagate downstream.
IF A-generated summaries are fed into B without validation, B may preserve or amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Validate A outputs against source documents.
Keep A outputs labeled as untrusted.
Compare B results against original inputs.
requires-engineering: add schema and citation checks before handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A explicitly handles configuration secrets and requests elevated privileges, while Agent B is a document-processing tool with privacy-policy and docs endpoints but no stated sensitive-data certifications or residency constraints. The main compliance concern is limited to handling A’s secrets in a broader processing workflow; no direct residency mismatch is evidenced, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Agent B's document pipeline, policy review is required.
IF Agent A secrets are stored in shared logs, retention controls must cover them.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces.
Review retention settings for logs and artifacts.
Keep secrets in dedicated secret stores.
Confirm privacy policy before uploading documents.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees.
